newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran-Gulf Arab cooperation prospects bright-Tehran.
newsitem.headline: Iran-Gulf Arab cooperation prospects bright-Tehran.

text.p: Prospects for cooperation between Iran and Gulf Arab states are bright, a senior Iranian official said in remarks published in Tehran on Tuesday.

Ali Asghar Khaji, Foreign Ministry director general for Persian Gulf affairs, said the Islamic republic was witnessing closer relations with Gulf littoral states due to cultural and historical common ground.

In an interview with the English-language daily Iran News he termed prospects for future cooperation bright and said: "It is time for regional states to lay a correct and logical foundation for resistance to foreign intervention and resolve their differences without foreign interference."
Khaji said that besides its status as an important regional waterway, the Gulf held 65 percent of known oil and 35 percent of world gas reserves.

Relations between non-Arab Iran and the conservative families who rule oil states on the Arab side of the Gulf have been strained since Shi'ite Moslem clerics led an Islamic revolution that toppled the Iranian monarchy in 1979.

The six Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Qatar and Bahrain -- have collectively accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs and are worried about an Iranian arms build-up.
Tehran says they have nothing to fear and do not need to rely on protection by the United States, which keeps a large military force in the region.
The Iranian official said there were still grounds for further collaboration between Iran and Kuwait, Oman and Qatar.

On trade relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, he said friendly negotiations were being conducted. And Iran would participate in an international trade fair in Saudi Arabia later this year.
Khaji said Iran could work with its southern neighbours in oil- and gas-related industries, environment control and especially in the preservation of aquatic species, he said.
